memory_candidates.content: The sanctioned errors.json writer (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/errors-append.sh) has an asymmetric mutation surface that shapes how error-triage close-out tasks must be planned: its `append` subcommand can set `severity` at creation time, but its `update` subcommand accepts ONLY --id, --fix-status, --fixed-date, and --fix-task. There is no sanctioned path to mutate an existing record's severity. Any task instruction phrased as 'downgrade severity from X to Y' is therefore unimplementable as written without either hand-editing specs/errors.json (forbidden -- the writer holds flock -x across read/transform/validate/mv and validates the MERGED document against context/schemas/errors-schema.json) or widening the writer's flag set (schema blast radius). The correct planning move is to close the record instead (--fix-status fixed --fix-task N): a closed record is out of triage regardless of its historical severity stamp, so closure delivers the downgrade's practical outcome and is strictly stronger. Plan the constraint check as an explicit first task with a Scope Hypothesis, so the implementer confirms the argument parser rather than trusting the plan's reading and reaching for a hand edit when the flag is rejected.
